observations: Multiple stacks of car batteries in retail cardboard packaging.
Brands 'RUNALL' (red boxes), 'SOLITE' (purple boxes), and 'ROCKET' (blue boxes) are visible.
The batteries are stacked on a paved outdoor surface.
Specific technical specifications like Ampere-hours (Ah) are not legible on the boxes.
Some boxes are wrapped in protective plastic film.

claims.evidence: The boxes appear intact and some are shrink-wrapped, but the actual batteries are not visible to confirm condition.
Authenticity of automotive parts cannot be confirmed through photos alone.
The Ah ratings on the boxes are too small to read in the provided photo.

risks.proof: A close-up photo of the label on the box or the battery itself showing the Ah rating.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the lowest standard capacity (e.g., 45Ah)

risks.risk: Battery may be old stock/expired shelf life
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturing date code stamped into the plastic casing of the battery.
risks.if_unproven: priced as old stock with reduced lifespan

risks.risk: Battery may be discharged or defective
risks.proof: A video showing a multimeter reading of the battery voltage (should be 12.6V or higher).

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the label on the specific battery of interest showing the Ah rating and model.
Photo of the manufacturing date code stamped on the battery casing.
Video of a multimeter test showing the current voltage of the battery.
response.reason: The capacity (Ah) and specific model numbers are not legible in the photo. Since car battery prices vary significantly based on these specs, a price cannot be determined without them.
